title: Dynamic Headroom Orchestrator with Safety Curtains
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Current autoscale policies for Dedicated fleets are brittle under mixed workloads (short chat bursts vs long-text generation). We see oscillations when using single-metric targets (p95 latency or token throughput alone) and occasional overshoot that triggers operator intervention. This ticket proposes a Dynamic Headroom Orchestrator (DHO): a pluggable policy component that composes multiple target metrics, computes transient headroom budgets, and enforces safety curtains (hard caps and decay windows) to prevent dangerous surges.

Goals:
- Define a canonical set of target metrics (p50/p95 latency, effective throughput tokens/s, GPU utilization, request concurrency) and their priority ordering per tenant class.
- Implement a scoring function that maps observed telemetry to a single scale-in/scale-out intention value with confidence bands.
- Add safety curtains: max-step-size, cool-down hysteresis, and budgeted surge credits that decay over time.
- Provide a simulation harness and CI smoke tests to validate no-regressions vs existing autoscaler for representative workloads.
- Expose user-configurable knobs in Dedicated UI and API for enterprise customers (min/max allocation, burst window size, allowed surge budget).

Design notes:
- Target composition: use a weighted quantile aggregator with tunable weights per route/fleet. Default weight set: {p95 latency: 0.45, throughput: 0.35, gpu_util: 0.15, concurrency: 0.05}. We expect product to iterate on defaults after cohort experiments.
- Scoring algorithm: normalized each metric to [0,1] using rolling baselines, then compute a weighted sum. Intention > 0.6 -> scale out, < 0.35 -> scale in. Thresholds are configurable.
- Safety curtains:
  1) step_limit: absolute max nodes added/removed per minute (default 20% of fleet size).
  2) surge_budget: temporary headroom (in vCPU/GPU units) that can be consumed for latency-critical workloads; budget decays exponentially with half-life = 30m.
  3) cooldown_window: prevents re-scaling within X seconds after a scale event unless emergency_flag set.
- Emergency fallback: if GPU OOMs or error rate > 5% and p95 latency worsening, automatically cap new requests (reject or queue) and open an incident.

Acceptance criteria:
- DHO implemented as a modular policy that can be plugged into the autoscale controller.
- End-to-end tests demonstrating stable behavior on 3 synthetic workloads (chat-bursty, steady high-throughput, mixed long-tail).
- Dashboard widgets for: headroom budget, recent scale events, safety curtain triggers, per-tenant score time-series.
- Backwards-compatible API: if customers do not opt-in, existing autoscaler behavior remains unchanged.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Weighting scheme complexity vs. user mental model: prefer sensible defaults and a small set of presets (cost-optimized, latency-first, balanced) instead of exposing many knobs.
- Surge budget fairness: whether to implement per-tenant proportional leasing (preserve high-commit customers) or global first-come model. Proposal: start with per-tenant proportional leasing based on committed capacity.
- Simulation fidelity vs. runtime complexity: rich simulators increase confidence but add maintenance cost. We'll keep simulator focused on realistic timeseries patterns and reuse traffic traces from prod (anonymized).

Implementation plan:
1) Spec and API doc (this ticket) -> Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/DHO+Spec (draft).
2) Library code: implement metric compositor and scoring in runtime/autoscaler/pkg/dho. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4829 (WIP).
3) Safety curtains engine in autoscaler control plane with feature flag rollout.
4) Simulator harness (python) under infra/simulators/dho_sim with 3 provided scenarios.
5) Console UI changes: new panel in Dedicated > Fleets. Design mockups in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/DHO-UI-Mockups.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Add metrics: dho_score{tenant}, dho_surgebudget{tenant}, dho_step_limit_triggered_total, dho_cooldown_skips_total.
- SLO target: reduce scale/float oscillations by > 60% on mixed workloads in A/B tests; maintain p95 within SLA 99% of time.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal fleets only (feature flag). Run for 2 weeks, collect regressions.
- Beta: opt-in for customers with Dedicated fleets. Monitor for 4 weeks.
- GA: default for new Dedicated clusters, opt-out available for 30 days post-launch.

Notes on safety & security: DHO only affects allocation signals; all control-plane RPCs validated with existing RBAC. Any changes that allow forced scale must pass security review.
